title: Token entropy–adjusted attribution window and shadow reconciler
creator: Anya Patel
description:
Problem:
Late-arriving usage events (edge logs, region tails, and occasional replayed client events) are causing both double-counting and missing token attributions across multi-route and multi-model requests. Current ledger pipeline applies simple dedupe by request_id and window watermarking which fails for: (1) interleaved sessions where identical request_ids are reused across micro-sessions, and (2) shards that report delayed KV cache evictions leading to attribution skew. Result: customers see occasional overcharges and credits applied after invoices go out, which is causing increased support tickets and trust erosion.

Goal:
Create a robust reconciliation component — "token shadow reconciler" — that (a) maintains strong idempotence for in-flight and late events, (b) applies an entropy-adjusted attribution window to probabilistically place ambiguous tokens into the correct billable window, and (c) supports a streaming-first fast path plus a batch backfill ABI for long-tail corrections. The reconciler must be safe to run in parallel to the existing pipeline (shadow mode) and produce diff reports before we flip the production ledger.

Design summary:
- Fast path: streaming micro-service that consumes the canonical usage stream (Kafka topic: usage.canonical.v2) and performs per-tenant sliding-window session stitching using a fingerprint composed of (tenant_id, partial_session_hash, time_bucket, route_family). To handle reused request_ids we introduce session_nonce and sequence heuristics.
- Entropy-adjusted windowing: compute an uncertainty score per event (based on inter-arrival jitter, route multiplicity, and token-length distribution). Use a configurable threshold to expand the attribution window for high-uncertainty groups and apply probabilistic fractional attribution when absolute assignment <= threshold. This reduces binary flip-flopping between adjacent windows.
- Shadow reconciler job: idempotent batch job (Spark/Beam) that reads raw events + fast-path outputs and emits a reconciled ledger delta with provenance tags (shadow_run_{timestamp}). The job includes a reconciliation confidence metric and a human-reviewable diff export (CSV + a pointer to the reconciliation dashboard).
- Consistency & guarantees: reconciler emits monotonic sequence tokens per-tenant to ensure downstream idempotence; it writes reconciliation checkpoints to the existing ledger-checkpoints store and supports resumable retries.
- Safety & rollout: start in shadow-only mode for 2 weeks on 10% of tenants (split by non-critical tiers). Create alerting for (1) reconciliation delta > 2% of tenant monthly usage, (2) any negative-billing deltas, (3) unmatched events older than 14 days.

Implementation tasks:
1) Proto: reconciliation proto additions for provenance tags and confidence score (backward compatible).
2) Streaming service: lightweight consumer with local state (LRU session cache + KV cache delta detector). Expose /health and /metrics.
3) Batch job: Beam pipeline that can run on GCP Dataflow or locally for tests.
4) Export: reconciliation diff S3 path and an ingestion shim to the Console reconciliation dashboard.
5) Tests: unit, integration in pre-prod with synthetic late-arrival scenarios, and a property-based test for idempotence.
6) Runbook: step-by-step for rollback, manual adjourn, and customer-facing credit issuance flow.

Trade-offs considered:
- Full deterministic reassignments vs probabilistic fractional attribution: deterministic logic was brittle on interleaved sessions; fractional attribution reduces hard flips but adds complexity for invoice presentation. We will keep invoices integerized by applying rounding policies and surface fractional reconciliations in the dashboard detail.
- Streaming-only design vs hybrid: streaming provides low-latency fixes but cannot fully heal historical tails; therefore hybrid (stream+batch) chosen.
- Complexity of session_nonce adoption: requires SDK changes for ideal correctness; we will implement heuristics for now and add SDK guidance as a follow-up (see sub-task).
Acceptance_criteria: Shadow reconciler produces reconciliation deltas for synthetic dataset with >95% attribution correctness compared to gold standard
Streaming fast-path runs at target P95 latency <= 200ms for 99th percentile tenant traffic
Reconciliation job is idempotent (re-running with same inputs yields no new deltas) verified by automated test
Diff export available in S3 and linked from reconciliation dashboard
Shadow mode active for the initial 10% tenant cohort without triggering safety alerts for two weeks
observability: Dashboard: billing.reconciliation.{tenant_id}.reconciler contains: backlog_size, delta_tokens, delta_cost_usd, confidence_histogram, late_event_age_p90. Alerts: recon.delta_pct_high, recon.negative_delta, recon.unmatched_old_events. Instrument per-stage timers and sample traces in Honeycomb for 1% of runs.
migration_plan: Phase 1: Deploy proto changes and batch job in shadow-only for 10% tenants. Phase 2: Run 14-day shadow sweep, analyze diffs, iterate thresholds. Phase 3: Enable corrective small credits for validated deltas < $50 and automated adjustments for deltas >= $50 after manual review. Phase 4: Flip reconciler into authoritative ledger with canary subset, monitor for 48 hours, then full rollout.
rollback_plan: Disable reconciler ingestion, stop batch jobs, run backfill compensator to revert any applied deltas, and push manual ledger correction if necessary. Pager escalation: on negative-billing delta alert, immediately pause reconciler and notify Customer Ops.
risks: SDK adoption lag for session_nonce increases chance of ambiguous attributions. Fractional attribution might require additional billing presentation work in Console to avoid customer confusion. Beam job resource spikes during extreme backfill may temporarily affect other pipelines—use reserved Dataflow quotas.
outstanding_decisions: 1) Final threshold for entropy-based window expansion (TBD after synthetic runs). 2) Rounding policy for fractional attributions (floor vs probabilistic rounding). 3) Whether to require SDK session_nonce before making reconciler authoritative.
